already-have.reason: Not implemented and not squarely contradicted. Only a RAM-resident slice exists: the PIN-attempt reason ring plus its PIN-less read command (CMD 4 / INS 0x03), the RCC_CSR reset-cause classifier (boot log only, sticky flags cleared), the TAMP reason decoder (secure_log only), TZIC VIOLATION_COUNT/LAST_SR (SRAM statics), and the #484 panic fatal screen (generic text, no reason, panic path only). HardFault and NMI zeroize and sys_reset with no register capture; `_ef` is unused. Nothing persists across a reset, nothing survives a wipe, and no fault-register snapshot exists. The persistence half is acknowledged as a follow-up in pin_attempt_log.rs:19-27 but has no GitHub issue. Three parts of the proposal collide with recorded constraints and need owner decisions rather than implementation: the PIN-less disclosure (#719 is still open, and persistence removes the "seized powered-off device yields nothing" argument it rests on), a new page-127 record class (page 127 is exclusively the first-boot journal + salt), and the "reason line after the FSBL fingerprint" (FSBL size/boot budget is the recorded NO-GO).
already-have.corrections:
1. Split the proposal. (a) Volatile capture of fault registers and TAMP/TZIC status, folded at next boot, is untracked and cheap. (b) A wipe-surviving public flash record is blocked on two owner decisions: #719 extended to persistence, and page ownership.

2. #719 changes materially. Its own risk argument and pin_attempt_log.rs:47-50 rely on the log being RAM-resident, so a seized powered-off device yields nothing. A wipe-surviving, PIN-less record removes that mitigation and leaves a durable owner-activity and tamper-history signal. This is a new decision, not an extension of the existing one.

3. Drop or re-home the "reason line after the FSBL fingerprint". The FSBL is pre-PIN and size-bounded (invariant #10; bench linker 32 KiB with a 28,704 B image; #540/#758 say the 5th page already costs the boot-state page). On pq1 the FSBL cannot even light the panel (#705), and the pq1 bench board has no LCD. Render the reason in the secure world instead (measured_boot screen or the #484 fatal screen), or expose it over the read-only CMD only.

4. Page 127 is not free. flash_policy.rs:30 and :177-185 fence the first-boot journal, and CLAUDE.md invariant #3 says page 127 owns the first-boot journal and salt. A public class there needs a flash-policy and model change, and must not weaken the Phase A "blank per-device pages 123-127" precondition of rdp2-self-lock. A record written before first boot, or surviving a wipe and re-provision, would break that blank check. The proposal's risk note misses this interaction.

5. The TAMP backup-register option depends on open ship-blockers #50 (backup-register secure-zone/privilege config) and #47 (hardware-mode tamper erase, tamp.rs base-address bug), and on #208. Under tamp-wipe the tamper path calls trigger_intrusion_wipe, so the snapshot must be ordered before it and stored outside the erased set.

6. The reset-cause capture half already exists (secure/src/reset_cause.rs, called at main.rs:1186). The gap is persistence and exposure in production, where secure_log is compiled out. sys_reset from HardFault classifies as Software, so fault resets are indistinguishable from deliberate ones today; that is the concrete delta.

7. Evidence citations #595 and #487 are irrelevant: #595 is the option-byte prodtest report and #487 is hw-model binding in the manifest. Only #715 and #719 are on point.

8. The "FI-sentinel trip", "SE link reset" and "ECC single-error" counters have no existing source counters in the tree that I found (not exhaustively searched). Treat them as new instrumentation, which pushes cost toward L if included. Recommend cutting them from the first version.

9. Naming: avoid "telemetry". #605 (closed) published a no-telemetry commitment for the companion; a device-local forensic record is not a conflict but should not be labelled telemetry.

10. Priority P1 is too high. Nothing ships until S-1/S-2/S-3 close, #75 (TAMP escalation) is the ship-blocker this depends on, and the proposal is diagnostics rather than a security control. P2, with the volatile-capture slice attachable to #715.

No issue tracks any of the following.

1. Capturing CFSR/HFSR/SFSR/SFAR/BFAR/MMFAR and the stacked PC in HardFault/NMI before sys_reset. The Trezor systask postmortem analog was never a row in the parity sweep or in #366.
2. Persisting the PIN-attempt reason ring at lockout. It is named as a follow-up only in the source comment at secure/src/pin_attempt_log.rs:23-27.

feasible.reason:
The code premise is true and the need is real, but SYS-06 is a diagnostic rather than a defence, and two of its three mechanisms are mis-specified. It needs no board change. Verdict: not refuted, with heavy corrections.

**Premise checks (all confirmed in code)**
- HardFault and NMI zeroize and reset without capturing anything (secure/src/main.rs:4651-4654, 4682-4690).
- The PIN-attempt ring is RAM-only and names persistence at lockout as its follow-up (secure/src/pin_attempt_log.rs:19-27).
- The TZIC violation counter and LAST_SR are SRAM statics (secure/src/hw/tzic.rs:83,88).
- The TAMP reason is decoded and logged only, and its flags are then cleared (secure/src/hw/tamp.rs:364-396).

**Mechanism 1 (capture medium) is wrong for the tamper case**
- There is no per-register "CR3-erased set". TAMP_CR3 is per-source no-erase, and pq1 writes CR3=0 (tamp.rs:301-307), so every enabled internal tamper is confirmed-mode and erases all TAMP_BKPxR.
- BKP0-7 already hold the BHK under BHKLOCK (secure/src/hw/bhk.rs:58,381-419); at most BKP8-31 are free.
- A snapshot written before the erase, or while the flag is still set, is lost. The handler would have to write after the SCR clear at tamp.rs:384. This rests on my recollection of RM0456, not a check in this session.
- The simpler source is TAMP_SR itself, which is backup-domain sticky. But `init` clears it unread (tamp.rs:272), throwing away the one tamper record that survives a reset.
- For faults, BKP8-31 or a no-init SRAM1 mailbox works across `sys_reset`. Secure RAM is SRAM1 at 0x30000000 (secure/memory-stm32u585-slot-a.x). No no-init section exists today, and startup plus the abnormal-reset scrub zero RAM, so linker and startup changes are needed.
- The ship option-byte SRAM_RST setting decides whether SRAM1 survives a reset; I did not verify it (only comments at secure/src/reset_cause.rs:97-98).

**Mechanism 2 (page 127) is the wrong page**
- Bank-1 page 127 is the append-only, never-erased first-boot journal (secure/src/flash_policy.rs:3-7; 512 quad-words, secure/src/first_boot/journal.rs:36).
- It holds the persisted TRNG salt that the final OPTIGA PBS derives from. Erasing or compacting the page is never safe.
- Appending attacker-triggerable records there gives a finite, non-reclaimable budget on the same page as load-bearing key material.
- No ECC-error handling exists in secure/ or fsbl/ (grep finds only comments; main.rs:4641-4643 says no NMI source is armed). A torn quad-word on that page could become a boot-time fault once ECCD-NMI lands.
- Every other per-device page is taken: 123 off-chain, 124 PIN, 125 admin/wipe/duress (erased at wipe finish, flash.rs:633), 126 wrapped BHK.
- The only unowned page is bank-2 page 127, which the frozen registry const-asserts must stay erased (geometry/src/lib.rs:106,137,291-295). Using it is a registry change plus a watermark and Phase-A blank-check change.

**Bypasses and overstatements**
1. A fault-injection attacker controls power. With no battery, cutting VDD after a glitch destroys the backup registers, SRAM and TAMP_SR before the boot-time fold. "FI is distinguishable from flaky hardware" holds only for events followed by a powered reboot.
2. NS can trigger SecureFaults at will. SHCSR is never written (no hits in secure/ or fsbl/), so all faults escalate to the one secure HardFault. Without saturating, first-fault-wins, bounded-write counters, the fold is a lever for flash wear and page fill.
3. Capturing the faulting PC with NS/S state means reading a stacked frame through NS MSP/PSP when the fault came from NS. cortex-m-rt's `ExceptionFrame` argument does not handle that. An unvalidated read published in a PIN-less record is a 4-byte secure-memory read oracle per fault; it needs a `cmse` TT range check or S-origin frames only.
4. The PIN-less disclosure argument rests on RAM residency: "being RAM-resident a seized powered-off device yields nothing" (pin_attempt_log.rs:48-50). Persisting the ring removes that argument, so this is a new owner decision, not an extension of #719.

**Feasibility on pq1**
- No hardware change; kind stays firmware.
- The read-only command already exists for the ring: CMD_GET_PIN_ATTEMPT_LOG = 4 and INS 0x03 (proto/src/lib.rs:123,1026; secure/src/nsc/cmd_pin_attempt_log.rs).
- Reset-cause classification already exists (secure/src/reset_cause.rs).
- "After the FSBL fingerprint" must mean the secure-world measured_boot screen. Putting a record parser in the FSBL adds code to a 32 KiB region already at about 28.7 KiB, and that code becomes immutable at RDP-2.
- The pq1 bench board has no LCD, so the display leg cannot be validated on the bench.
- The ui-px image is already 76,949 B over the secure slot; this adds a small amount more.
feasible.corrections:
**Required changes to the proposal**
1. Drop "backup registers NOT in the CR3-erased set". All BKP registers are erased on a confirmed tamper and BKP0-7 are BHK-locked. For tamper, read and fold TAMP_SR at boot before the clear at tamp.rs:272. Alternatively, write a reason from the handler after the SCR clear at tamp.rs:384.
2. For faults, use BKP8-31 or a no-init SRAM1 mailbox with magic and CRC. This needs a new linker section and an exemption from the abnormal-reset scrub. Verify the ship option-byte SRAM_RST setting first.
3. Do not use bank-1 page 127. It is the append-only journal holding the OPTIGA PBS salt. Take an explicit page decision; the only candidate is bank-2 page 127 (ReservedErased, geometry/src/lib.rs:137,291-295). That means a frozen-registry change, a secure-watermark check, a Phase-A blank-check update, and the flash-policy/Verus/TLA+ updates.
4. Pages 124 and 125 cannot host the record; both are erased by the wipe.
5. Bound the writes: saturating counters (for example log2 buckets), first-fault-wins, and a hard lifetime cap on quad-words. NS can trigger SecureFault and HardFault at will.
6. Capture the PC only for secure-origin frames, or TT-validate the NS stack pointer before reading. Never copy stacked register contents. Capture after `zeroize_sensitive_state`.
7. State the scope honestly: evidence exists only for events followed by a powered reboot. A power-cut attack leaves nothing on a board with no battery.
8. Render the reason in the secure-world measured_boot screen, not the FSBL. The FSBL is about 28.7 of 32 KiB and frozen at RDP-2; a parser of attacker-influenced data does not belong there.
9. Persisting the ring invalidates the RAM-residency argument at pin_attempt_log.rs:48-50. This needs a fresh owner decision.
10. Reuse what exists: CMD 4 / INS 0x03 and reset_cause.rs. A torn write on the new page must not become a boot loop, since there is no ECC-error handling today.

**Trezor precedent errors**
- systask.c:96-102 is the SHCSR fault-enable code, not the postmortem. First-fault-wins is at about 522-527, inside the cited 509-560 range.
- That postmortem is a RAM structure shown on the RSOD. It is not persisted to backup RAM.
- The telemetry PUBLIC item holds only battery min/max temperature, battery error bits and cycles. It contains no fault or tamper data.
- "Survives wipe" there means surviving `backup_ram_erase_protected`, not a tamper erase. Trezor's backup SRAM also relies on BREN plus a battery (core/embed/sys/startup/stm32u5/startup_init.c:265), which pq1 lacks.
- The guard-NOK → payload → CRC → guard-OK journaling is at backup_ram.c:248-278, not 153-265 (151-166 is `backup_ram_erase`).
- tamper.c:209-248 (reason names) and telemetry.c:27-105 are accurate.
- "Parity" is overstated: Trezor has no persisted fault or tamper forensics either.

**Cost and priority**
- Cost is L, not M: page and registry decision, flash-policy and formal-model updates, linker and startup changes, custom fault trampoline, bounded-write codec, host tooling.
- Priority is P2: this is diagnostic, not a defence. The TAMP_SR read-before-clear and BKP fault snapshot exposed over the existing command are a cheap P1-worthy slice for #715.

- `tamp::init` clears TAMP_SR without reading it (tamp.rs:272), discarding the only tamper evidence that survives a reset; a read-and-fold before the clear is a few lines.
